runners_data.name: Paris Babe
runners_data.note: Archie Watson runner in good nick (1/21 T14), suited by 7f on Standard at Kempton with solid sim-going form (1W2P), wears headgear and should slot prominently just off the two leaders; 26 days since last run is fine.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Paris Babe nonetheless rates highest of the ten runners on our figures, with a speed rating of 88 backing that assessment, and she has run over today's trip before; the trainer's current 5% strike rate is a minor concern.

runners_data.name: Musical Angel
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who will go straight to the lead under Harry Davies, though sim-going figures on Standard are thin (0W0P in 3 runs) and the 41-day break is a mild flag for fitness sharpness.|
runners_data.comment: Musical Angel showed she can win with a victory five starts back, and her return to today's trip and going gives her a solid platform — the main concern is whether a third last time out represents her best after 41 days off.

runners_data.name: Bridget's View
runners_data.note: Rossa Ryan takes over on this genuine hold-up filly (hg:htp), who has consistent Kempton Standard form (2W2P in 7 sim-going runs) and was back out just 14 days ago — will need clear daylight to land her challenge from off the pace.|
runners_data.comment: Bridget's View has run over today's trip and going, arrives on a quick 14-day turnaround, and our rating of 87 marks her out as a genuine threat to the top-rated runner; the concern is that she has been winless in her last six starts.

runners_data.name: Star Mirage
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon takes the ride on this lightly-raced 3yo who has placed twice at 7f on Standard, but her sim-going record is narrow (1 run) and a 0 last time out on Good at Goodwood raises a query about recent form.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Star Mirage faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's distance and going before and returns on the back of two placed efforts in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Shushu
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's 3yo is a genuine front-runner who will dispute the lead with Musical Angel; the 63-day break is the principal concern, and her three-run career record is all on Soft or Good-to-Soft, making Standard to Slow an unknown quantity.|
runners_data.comment: Landed a win two starts back and was second three starts back, but a fifth last time out clouds her recent form; she has run over today's trip and a 63-day absence leaves fitness to prove.

runners_data.name: Merry
runners_data.note: James Horton's 3yo has strong Kempton Standard form (5 runs, 1W3P) and was out just 7 days ago showing freshness — in reality a natural prominent racer who will find early positions fiercely contested in this field, meaning the style-fit discount applies to its chance of getting its ideal pitch.|
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving her solid claims, but a mark of 72 and our rating suggesting only mid-division quality among this field keeps her squarely in the each-way bracket, with just the one win in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Ribenska
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes runner who is naturally prominent (hg:p) and has solid sim-going placed form (1W5P in 8 runs), but returns from 69 days off and may lack the sharpness to fight through a crowded early prominent group.|
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and a second three starts back, Ribenska brings some recent encouragement, though she remains winless in her last five starts and returns after a 69-day break; experience over today's trip and going gives her a footing, but she must bounce back from patchy form either side of that placed effort.

runners_data.name: Afraj
runners_data.note: William Buick aboard this Gosden 3yo who won at 7f on Standard and has consistent placed form — the booking of Buick is the sharpest jockey angle in the race and she should travel prominently without being embroiled in the lead duel.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked ninth of ten on our figures, Afraj makes it hard to build a case — a fourth last time out and a rating of 71 leave her up against it here, though she has run over today's trip and her trainer is in sharp form at 26% over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Ghisa
runners_data.note: Paddy Bradley on this genuine hold-up 3yo (hg:h) trained by Charlie Fellowes; two wins in sim-going (2W4P in 7 runs) suggests she handles the surface, but from the back she needs the pace duel to truly take its toll on those ahead.|
runners_data.comment: Twice third in her last two starts, Ghisa arrives on a sharp 26-day turnaround with experience over today's trip and an eye-catching rating of 85 that suggests she is better than her official mark; the risk is that she remains winless in recent starts and must prove she can convert her placed efforts.

runners_data.name: Sahana
runners_data.note: David Simcock's 4yo hold-up filly with a narrow sim-going profile (1W2P) and Dylan Hogan claiming; OR 68 is the lowest in the field and she will need significant late gaps to be competitive from her rearward position.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Sahana faces a stiff task here; a second three starts back offers a crumb of comfort, and she has run over today's distance and going before, but the overall profile makes her hard to fancy.

races.paceDynamic: Musical Angel and Shushu are the two confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the gates at Kempton's 7f start, creating a genuinely contested early gallop that is unlikely to collapse into a dawdle on Standard to Slow ground. Paris Babe, Star Mirage, Ribenska, and Afraj all want prominent positions, generating a congested early order that will compress the field through the first two furlongs and create meaningful traffic danger approaching the home turn two to three furlongs out. The field holds more prominent types than can all realistically hold that position — Musical Angel and Shushu are most likely to actually secure the lead, with Paris Babe and Afraj best placed to slot in just behind given their pace and handlers, while Ribenska and Star Mirage risk being squeezed back further than ideal. An honest-to-contested gallop on a flat track typically sets up horses with a prominent pitch who can travel smoothly in the slipstream and finish off — the pace-pressure scenario marginally favours those who can race just off the speed without burning energy early, rather than true hold-up types who will need significant gaps to open late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Musical Angel and Shushu fight for the front and sustain an honest gallop, burning off rivals by the home turn.
scenarios.body: The pace duel stretches the field, rewarding horses just off the speed who travel within themselves and have a sharp turn of foot for Kempton's straight. Prominent raiders who are not embroiled in the early battle inherit a perfect position rounding into the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Musical Angel or Shushu asserts early and the other capitulates, producing a controlled solo lead with a moderate gallop.
scenarios.body: A lone leader at a sustainable tempo on flat Kempton ground can simply dictate and not be run off their legs, making it difficult for hold-up horses to generate enough momentum late. The front-runner gets a soft lead and the tailwind of Standard to Slow ground helping them stay on.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the early duel burns both leaders out by the home turn and the mid-pack traffic jams stall prominent horses, opening a late run.
scenarios.body: Hold-up types who have saved energy through the first five furlongs get a clear passage and pick off the toiling early leaders in the final furlong on tiring ground. Bridget's View and Ghisa, who are genuine hold-up operators, are best positioned to capitalise if gaps materialise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Shuffled Through
scenarios.trigger: If traffic chaos two to three out disrupts the prominent group and a horse from deep midfield threads through late.
scenarios.body: With four horses scrapping for early position, any checks or switches mid-race can gift an advantage to a horse who avoids trouble by sitting off the pace entirely. This is a low-probability outcome as true hold-up form in this field is limited and the pace is unlikely to be severe enough to produce a decisive finishing burst from far back.

watchPoints.text: Musical Angel and Shushu are both confirmed front-runners — watch for an aggressive early duel that could see both weakened inside the final two furlongs, dramatically opening up the race for prominent trackers.|

Four horses (Paris Babe, Star Mirage, Ribenska, Afraj) are all seeking prominent positions behind the lead pair — congestion two to three furlongs out is a serious risk and any horse trapped wide or checked at that point loses ground it may not recover on a flat track.|

Shushu returns from 63 days off for Roger Varian with no form on Standard going — if she fails to stride out naturally early, Musical Angel could be left in front alone, fundamentally altering the race shape and reducing the pace pressure.|

William Buick's booking on Afraj (John & Thady Gosden, OR 76) stands out as the most significant jockey-trainer angle in the race — his ability to find a prominent pitch without over-committing early is worth noting in a contested scenario.|

Bridget's View was out just 14 days ago for Stuart Williams, suggesting she is race-fit and ready, but Rossa Ryan will need clean passage from her hold-up draw as the field is likely to string out quickly once the lead duel ignites.|

races.name: Try Unibet's New Improved Acca Boosts Fillies' Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Gloryous
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who will press for the lead from flag-fall; trainer Jamie Osborne in fair form (T14: 2/12) but sim-going record of 0W0P in 2 runs is a concern, and this Standard to Slow surface may blunt her finishing effort after duelling with Bintknight.
runners_data.comment: Gloryous has been knocking on the door in recent starts, with a second last time out and a third two starts back suggesting she is in fine fettle, and a rating of 91 puts her clearly ahead of her rivals here; consistent but yet to win in her last five, she has the profile to finally get her head in front.

runners_data.name: Aphrodite Spirit
runners_data.note: Roger Teal's 4yo has solid credentials over this 14f trip — a winner at 10f on Standard and placed third here over 14f at Goodwood — her 1W1P on similar going makes her a serious contender if she tracks the pace comfortably from a prominent pitch.
runners_data.comment: Aphrodite Spirit showed a nice turn of foot when winning three starts back, and her flanking placings suggest consistency, though she has been off 40 days and a mark of 76 with 138 lb to carry may test her here.

runners_data.name: Ladykirk
runners_data.note: William Buick takes the ride for Jane Chapple-Hyam, who is in strong form (T14: 3/14); Ladykirk holds a genuine hold-up style and placed second over 12f on Standard recently — Buick's positioning from a patient berth in the straight is this filly's primary weapon.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked seventh of eight on our figures, Ladykirk faces a stiff ask under 135 lb, though she has run over today's trip and a second last time out shows she retains some ability.

runners_data.name: Bint Kilfrush
runners_data.note: James Tate's 3yo carries a 109-day layoff into this and will need to show freshness is a positive rather than a negative; her sim-going record of 1W1P from 3 runs is encouraging, and if fit she has the late-running profile to benefit from the front-runners tiring.
runners_data.comment: Bint Kilfrush advertises a win three starts back and our rating of 85 marks her as a genuine threat in this field, though the 109-day absence is the obvious query heading into this contest.

runners_data.name: Big Bear Hug
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle's 7yo is a genuine hold-up horse by inclination, though the crowded rear-of-field means she is less likely to find her true position — her sim-going record from 15 runs (1W1P) is modest, and at OR 71 she faces a stiff task on a track where passage can be tricky with a big field.
runners_data.comment: Big Bear Hug won three starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, with our rating of 82 marking her out as a leading threat in this field; the concern is consecutive seventh-place finishes since that victory.

runners_data.name: Bintknight
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton's progressive 3yo has won twice at 10f on Good and twice placed, arriving on a four-race sequence of 5-1-2-1 — she will push hard for the lead and if Gloryous cannot match strides, Bintknight's recent confidence and youth could prove decisive over the longer 14f.
runners_data.comment: Bintknight arrives on the back of a win last time out, with an encouraging record of two wins in her last four starts showing she knows how to find the line; the 132 lb burden is a stern ask, however, and her speed rating leaves a little to find on our figures.

runners_data.name: Affection
runners_data.note: David Pipe's 3yo is a natural hold-up filly whose recent form includes a win over 10f and a placing over 17f at Goodwood — displaced toward midfield on the map due to the congested rear, she may not find the clean late run her style demands, which tempers confidence despite the solid form figures.
runners_data.comment: Affection won two of her last six starts, and a third two runs back underlines her consistency at this level; our rating of 86 supports her claims as a serious threat, though the fourth last time out raises a question about her current peak.

runners_data.name: Seacole
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett holds excellent overall form (T14: 6/37) and Rossa Ryan takes over in the saddle; Seacole has placed in all three career starts (2-4-2) and holds headgear (h), suggesting she has enough tactical tractability to sit in behind and attack late — her consistency makes her a key player.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Seacole faces a stiff ask off 130 lb, though she has run over today's trip before and consecutive runner-up finishes either side of a fourth show she is capable of running her race.

races.paceDynamic: Gloryous and Bintknight are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off over this 1m4f trip on a Standard to Slow Kempton surface, creating a genuine, honest pace rather than a falsely run dawdle. Gloryous brings recent experience at Goodwood and has placed off front-running tactics, while Bintknight arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and is unlikely to surrender the rail without a fight — expect these two to push each other through the early stages and set up a true test of stamina in the straight. The contested pace over a middle-distance trip on this track profile strongly favours hold-up or late-finishing types who can conserve energy through the first mile and unleash a sustained run in the Kempton straight, particularly horses with proven stamina and a clean passage. The field carries more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear — Affection and Big Bear Hug are genuine late-runners by nature but have been displaced into midfield positions on the map, making it less certain they will find their ideal spot; Ladykirk and Seacole are most likely to secure genuine rear-tracking berths and benefit most cleanly from the contested pace set by the two leaders.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Land
scenarios.trigger: If Gloryous and Bintknight fight for the lead and set a genuine gallop that stretches the field turning in.
scenarios.body: The sustained tempo drains the front-runners through the final two furlongs, leaving the straight open for horses held up or tracking in midfield to reel them in; stamina-proven hold-up types with a Kempton straight to aim at are ideally placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leads, Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Bintknight breaks best and Gloryous is unable to match strides, leaving one horse to control pace on its own terms.
scenarios.body: A solo leader setting a controlled, moderate gallop could preserve enough in the tank to hold on late, particularly if the straight is attacked at the right moment; Bintknight's recent winning form and youth give it the profile to do this.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If Aphrodite Spirit or another prominent type tracks the leaders in a prime position and benefits from a slight easing of pace mid-race.
scenarios.body: A horse racing in second or third on the bridle takes a decisive move two furlongs out before the true hold-up runners can get fully organised; Aphrodite Spirit's 1W1P on similar going and proven form over 14f make her a natural fit for this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Fail, Pace Collapses
scenarios.trigger: If both front-runners overcook the pace early then fade, creating a vacuum in the straight that allows a midfield stalker to coast through.
scenarios.body: A horse racing comfortably in the middle of the field avoids the early battle and picks up the pieces as the leaders stop in front of them; Seacole's consistent placing form and hold-up tendencies give her a plausible route through.

watchPoints.text: Gloryous and Bintknight are on a collision course for the lead — watch the first two furlongs closely to see which establishes control, as the outcome of that duel will shape the entire race.

Ladykirk with William Buick aboard could be dangerously underrated — if Buick settles her cleanly off the pace and the front-runners fight themselves into submission, she has the profile and jockey to produce a late challenge.

Bint Kilfrush returns from 109 days off and any signs of ring-rustiness early could be costly in a race where position will be won and lost fast with two confirmed front-runners; watch her behaviour in the stalls and early strides.

Affection and Big Bear Hug are genuine hold-up horses squeezed toward midfield by the shape of this field — if either finds a clear passage sweeping wide into the straight they should not be ignored, but a troubled run is a real risk.

The Standard to Slow going description for this race (7:51 1m4f) is slightly softer than earlier races on the card — monitor final going reports as any further deterioration would favour stamina-heavy profiles and disadvantage horses who rely on a quick surface.

races.name: Unibet 3 Uniboosts A Day Handicap Stakes (London Sprint Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Aigeas
runners_data.note: Won over this exact C&D trip on Standard going 55 days ago (sim-going strike rate 2W from 5 runs) and returns to ideal conditions; hold-up style keeps him out of the early traffic war entirely, meaning he arrives fresh at the death when the pace-setters are emptying.
runners_data.comment: Aigeas won last time out and has experience of today's distance and going, which counts in his favour; however, he was well beaten in three of his four starts before that, and 55 days off the track leaves a fitness question at 135 lb from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Wezzeer
runners_data.note: Roger Varian 7/19 in last 14 days and this colt has won twice at 6f on Standard AW; 74 days off is the one query, but prominent style suits a race where the pace will be fast enough to track into without forcing it — Ray Dawson keeps this simple.
runners_data.comment: Wezzeer won three starts back and was second two starts ago, making him the one to beat on his recent form, and he has run over today's trip and going before; the 74-day absence is the only note of caution, but his 135 lb burden and draw two are straightforward facts to work with.

runners_data.name: Caviar Cowboy
runners_data.note: Exceptional sim-going record (6 from 7 placings on comparable surfaces) and has placed on every AW start; presses from a prominent berth and Daniel Muscutt will look to exploit any daylight that the early lead fight opens up — headgear (h) worn.
runners_data.comment: Caviar Cowboy shaped with promise when runner-up three starts back and went one better with a win four starts back, and he has experience of today's trip and going to call upon; the risk is that he has not recaptured that form in his last two outings.

runners_data.name: Society Kiss
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner dropping from 5f to 6f for the first time, which is the key unknown — she has won at 5f on Standard but has never proved she can maintain that early pace over an extra furlong on AW; PJ McDonald gives this a chance if she fires.
runners_data.comment: Society Kiss shaped with real promise when third two starts back and followed up with a runner-up finish last time out, suggesting she's hitting her stride, and she has run over today's trip; the main concern is the 79-day absence since that encouraging effort.

runners_data.name: Arry Up
runners_data.note: Three wins from nine on Standard going and happy at 6f; prominent style means he must survive the congested early stages without getting squeezed, but Rod Millman's yard is 2/19 in the last fortnight which tempers enthusiasm.
runners_data.comment: Ranked nine of eleven on our figures, Arry Up faces a stiff ask at the weights carrying 132 lb, and a speed rating of 73 underlines the concern; in his favour, he has run over today's trip and going before, and has shown a winning habit with three wins in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Augustus Gloop
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse from the Fanshawe yard (same trainer as Caviar Cowboy) that has placed in a 6f STA race previously; recent form figures (8,4,7,6,2) show inconsistency but the 2nd on Standard two runs ago signals he stays the trip — 19-day turnaround is short.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Augustus Gloop has experience of today's trip and conditions in his favour, but a sequence of 8th, 4th and 7th in recent outings gives pause, and 130 lb from stall six adds to the challenge for a gelding rated 84.

runners_data.name: Manly Fireball
runners_data.note: Genuine front-runner with one 6f STA win and a string of placed efforts on this surface (sim-going 8 from 9 runs); Richard Hughes 4/29 recently is moderate, but if Manly Fireball slots onto the rail early he can force rivals wide — stamina at the trip is proven.

runners_data.name: Bintaryana
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose single Standard-going appearance produced only one placing from six; Cieren Fallon will want a clean break given she must compete for prominent slots with at least four other horses — the sim-going record (0W, 1P from 6) does not inspire at this surface.
runners_data.comment: Bintaryana arrives on the back of a lively recent profile — a winner two starts back and a runner-up in two of her last five outings — and has run over today's trip, with 29 days between runs; the unplaced effort last time is the one concern to weigh up.

runners_data.name: King Of Chaos
runners_data.note: Three wins from nine on Standard (best sim-going record in the field by volume), all at 6f — this trip is his sweet spot; hold-up style under Pat Dobbs means he sidesteps the early brawl entirely, and Dylan Cunha is 5/22 in form, making this an each-way player in a burn-up.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom but one on our figures and with a patchy profile of two wins in his last six starts, King Of Chaos faces a stiff ask, though he does return on a fresh 26-day break, has run over today's trip, and that winning thread keeps him marginally interesting.

runners_data.name: Kolkata Knight
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner fitted with a tongue-tie; his five turf runs were all on Good-or-softer grass and produced zero wins, so this AW switch on Standard-to-Slow is an unknown quantity — PLJ Jamin has only one sim-going placing from 11 efforts behind him.
runners_data.comment: Kolkata Knight arrives here 12 days fresh and has run over today's trip, yet he remains winless in his last six starts, with a second six starts back his standout effort; fifth last time out and fourth three starts back suggest mid-division consistency without the finishing punch to threaten.

runners_data.name: Slay Queen
runners_data.note: Five consecutive out-of-the-places finishes, all on Good or Soft turf, with no AW experience at all — hold-up style is fine for the pace scenario but there is no evidence she handles this surface or translates turf form here; Richard Hannon yard 2/47 is poor.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Slay Queen faces a stiff ask here, with a trainer in poor form at 2/47 over the past fortnight doing little to inspire confidence, despite some distance experience and 44 days to freshen up.

runners_data.name: From The Hip
runners_data.note: Three 6f STA wins in recent form (sim-going 2W from 8) make the surface record compelling; prominent style suits if the pace gaps open ahead, but 79 days off and a cold trainer (0/12 in 14 days) for Mark Usher means fitness is the question Tyler Heard must answer early.
runners_data.comment: Winner three starts back and a third two starts back give From The Hip a solid recent profile, though 79 days off the track and a speed rating of 67 from draw 11 suggest he faces a stiff ask returning to action at 126 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Society Kiss, Manly Fireball, and Kolkata Knight all want to lead, guaranteeing a strong early gallop over this 6f Kempton AW straight, compounded further by Wezzeer, Caviar Cowboy, Arry Up, and Bintaryana all pressing for prominent positions — that is five horses chasing three or four berths, creating a compressed, scrappy break from the gates. The pace-setters will not be allowed to dictate cheaply; they will be harried throughout and the sectionals will be punishing, meaning stamina and the ability to finish through fatigue rather than off a false pace are the decisive qualities tonight. Standard-to-Slow going (confirmed for the 8:21 6f) will stretch the field further, rewarding horses who settle efficiently in the early stages and travel without fighting for position. This race shape firmly favours hold-up and closing profiles — Aigeas, Augustus Gloop, King Of Chaos, and Slay Queen can all bypass the early traffic war and arrive with momentum when the pace-setters are beginning to tie up in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Burn-Up Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners fight hard for the lead and collectively set a suicidal early pace, draining the prominent brigade before halfway.
scenarios.body: The lead trio — Society Kiss, Manly Fireball, Kolkata Knight — burn each other out by the 3f pole, and the hold-up horses sweep past a spent front rank in the final furlong; the Standard-to-Slow surface amplifies the energy cost of that early battle.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Survive
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner establishes a clear early lead and the pace settles into a strong-but-controlled gallop, allowing a prominent tracker to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: One of the lead trio — most likely Society Kiss or Manly Fireball — gets an uncontested berth on the inside rail and the gallop becomes controlled enough that a prominent horse like Wezzeer or Caviar Cowboy can track at a safe distance and pounce; the Standard-to-Slow ground suits those who travel smoothly rather than fight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Blocked
scenarios.trigger: If the early scramble creates a traffic-heavy race with hold-up horses unable to find daylight through a tightly packed field two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: The closers — Aigeas and King Of Chaos — are caught in the traffic jam that the pace dynamic explicitly flags between the 2f and 3f marker, leaving the race to a more prominent horse who managed to thread through cleanly; Caviar Cowboy's high sim-going strike rate at this venue makes it a logical beneficiary.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner jumps supremely well and the rivals behind them become too embroiled in their own battle to mount an organised pursuit.
scenarios.body: Society Kiss drops in trip from 5f where she has won, and if she fires quickly out of the gate she could find herself with daylight while Manly Fireball and Kolkata Knight neutralise each other; Standard-to-Slow ground increases the margin for error for an unchallenged leader if the chasing pack leaves the pursuit too late.

watchPoints.text: Society Kiss, Manly Fireball, and Kolkata Knight — watch which of the three gets cleanest early position; the one who leads without being harassed becomes a live runner, while the other two risk burning reserves fighting for the rail.
Aigeas and King Of Chaos — both hold-up horses must negotiate the traffic pocket flagged between 2f-3f out; if the field compresses at that point, neither may get a clear run until it is too late.

Kolkata Knight — tongue-tie first time on AW after five turf runs, all on Good or softer; if the surface does not suit, he adds to the early pace without being a genuine threat and simply inflates the burn-up for others.

From The Hip — 79 days off for a yard that is 0/12 in the last fortnight; early movement and how settled Tyler Heard can keep him in the first quarter-mile will tell you quickly whether this is a fit return or a prep run.

Standard-to-Slow confirmed for this 6f slot — expect times to run slower than advertised Standard benchmarks, which adds a further stamina premium and should slightly extend the advantage of horses who settle in the first half of the race.

races.name: Unibet More Extra Place Races Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Traveling Man
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Charlie Fellowes whose best form includes a win at 1m2f on Good, so the step to 1m4f here is an interesting test; jockey Paddy Bradley is an apprentice claim that helps, but this horse genuinely comes from off the pace and needs the closers' scenario to play out.
runners_data.comment: Traveling Man arrives on the back of a win last time out, though a sixth three starts back and a ninth in recent starts temper enthusiasm; he has run over today's trip and our rating of 72 offers mild support, but 135 lb is no light burden.

runners_data.name: Relentless Hero
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's yard is in excellent form at T14 (13/67) and Jason Watson is a solid booking, but Relentless Hero has no wins or places on similar going (0W0P in 6 sim-going runs) and races from hold-up position, making him reliant on a scenario that may not materialise.
runners_data.comment: Relentless Hero won three starts back and returns on a quick 18-day turnaround with distance and going experience in his favour, but he has to bounce back from a pair of below-par efforts since that victory and 134 lb is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Cosmo Brown
runners_data.note: William Muir and Chris Grassick have one runner in the past 14 days and Callum Shepherd is a capable claimer; races from the back in the style of a proper hold-up horse and has placed at 1m2f-1m4f on Good, so the trip suits but he needs the race to develop in his favour.
runners_data.comment: Cosmo Brown catches the eye on the back of a third last time out, and his rating of 74 gives him a clear edge over most rivals here; yet to win in recent starts, the main concern is whether he can convert that consistency into something more decisive off 134 lb.

runners_data.name: Madjid
runners_data.note: Won last time out at 1m2f on Good for Harry Charlton and Lewis Edmunds takes the ride; sim-going record of 0W0P in eight attempts on similar conditions is a concern, and 39 days off means fitness will be tested — races from the rear and needs something to happen in front of him.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win in his last six starts but has mixed form either side of it, and 39 days off adds a fitness query; rated 70 on our figures and the 133 lb burden is no help to his cause.

runners_data.name: Hot Silk
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's filly has placed on the all-weather (including a second over 1m3f at Kempton) and has placed on similar going; she is a genuine hold-up type operating out of her natural position in what the map shows as midfield, and the crowded rear means she may never find the clear run she needs.
runners_data.comment: Consistently placed in recent starts, Hot Silk arrives here just 16 days after finishing second, has run over today's trip, and our rating of 73 suggests she is ahead of the handicapper; the risk is that she remains yet to win in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Semper Femina
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's filly has placed on similar going (0W1P) and Pat Dobbs is a strong jockey booking; her natural home is behind the field, but the volume of back-markers in this race means she is shunted into a mid-division slot where she will be racing out of character.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and a second three starts back, Semper Femina arrives here in decent nick after a 35-day break, with experience over today's trip and going working in her favour; a trainer in lean form is the one reservation about this top-rated filly.

runners_data.name: Amrum
runners_data.note: William Buick is an elite booking for Ollie Sangster's yard and Amrum won over 1m2f on Good last time; 63 days off is the main flag, and as a hold-up horse that the field size has displaced into midfield, she needs a stronger pace than Evening Fades is likely to set.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win two starts back but has been well held either side of it, and 63 days off the track adds an unknown fitness element; he rates a shade above his official mark of 64 and holds a useful edge on our rating, though the weight of 129 lb is no help.

runners_data.name: Far Far Out
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's gelding has a finishing pattern that already flags late fading, and 58 days since his last run compounds the fitness query; bumped into midfield by the sheer weight of back-markers in this field, he is likely to find the task hardest if the race lacks a strong gallop.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, with back-to-back eighths his most recent efforts, Far Far Out is hard to fancy here — though he has run over today's trip and returns after 58 days, which at least suggests connections feel he is ready.

runners_data.name: Evening Fades
runners_data.note: William Haggas's filly is the lone confirmed front-runner with a second at Kempton over 1m4f on Standard going in her history, giving her a clear course-and-distance clue; on Standard To Slow tonight she can dictate without any genuine pace rival, though her record suggests she tends to find one or two finishing past her.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Evening Fades has been placed just once in that sequence — a second last time out — but has otherwise struggled to get into the mix, and our figures rank her towards the foot of this field.

runners_data.name: Lord Mayor
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding has excellent recent form (13/67) and PJ McDonald is a top jockey, but 197 days off is a serious fitness concern for a horse returning from a long layoff; his five sim-going runs have produced three places (0W3P) so the surface suits, and he races in mid-division where, if fit, he could get a prominent enough pitch.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after a 197-day absence, Lord Mayor faces a stiff ask ranked ninth of twelve on our figures, though he has experience of today's trip and conditions, and three consecutive thirds suggest he can at least hit the frame.

runners_data.name: Tinsel
runners_data.note: Won over 1m2f at Kempton on Standard and is four-from-eight (1W1P) on similar going, giving him a solid course profile; Callum Hutchinson is a claiming apprentice but the trainer Hughie Morrison has only one runner in the last 14 days — as a hold-up horse pushed into the mid-division by this crowded field, he still knows Kempton and the trip.
runners_data.comment: Tinsel won three starts back but has been off the mark since, finishing fourth and then ninth in his two most recent outings, so he arrives on a downward curve. He has run over today's trip and going, and 30 days fresh at 127 lb leaves him with something to prove.

runners_data.name: Cospicua
runners_data.note: James Tate's filly has a strong sim-going record (2W2P from nine runs) and won over 1m4f on Standard at Kempton previously, making her one of the best-qualified horses for today's surface and trip; she is a hold-up horse by nature and the map places her in mid-division, yet her proven course-and-distance form makes her dangerous if the closers' shape emerges.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and her recent form reads 5th, 6th, 6th in her last three starts, making her hard to fancy despite two wins in her last six; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 18 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh.

races.paceDynamic: Evening Fades is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 12-strong field, and on Standard To Slow Kempton polytrack over 1m4f she should be able to bowl along at a comfortable, unhurried tempo with no genuine rival to press her early. That controlled lead will stretch the race into a one-pace procession down the back and around the final bend, setting up a test of stamina and position rather than a brutal closing sprint. The field is saturated with hold-up horses — Hot Silk, Semper Femina, Amrum, Far Far Out, Lord Mayor, Tinsel and Cospicua are all genuine back-of-the-field operators who cannot all occupy the deep rear, meaning several will be forced into unfamiliar midfield slots that suit neither their racing pattern nor their finishing acceleration. With a solitary front-runner setting a sustainable gallop and the closers crowded out of their natural positions, this race shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield horses who can travel just behind Evening Fades and pounce as the pace eases into the straight, rather than true hold-up types who need a strong gallop to come from last.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Solo Leader Gifts Prominent
scenarios.trigger: If Evening Fades bowls along unchallenged and the pack settles into a falsely slow rhythm, allowing a well-positioned horse to cruise into contention.
scenarios.body: Evening Fades controls tempo completely and the race becomes a processional test of who is best placed rounding the final bend; horses that sit second or third and travel kindly will have first run on the tiring backmarkers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver From Mid
scenarios.trigger: If the Standard To Slow surface and 1m4f trip create enough genuine end-to-end stamina demands that well-held midfield horses grind past a wilting leader.
scenarios.body: Evening Fades's lead is taken up enough to string out the field, and the redistributed hold-up types who end up in mid-division are close enough to pounce in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Evening Fades goes too fast too soon on the slow-ish surface and blows up entering the straight, leaving everything to a late rattle.
scenarios.body: A strong pace leaves horses that were forced into midfield suddenly with the race in front of them at the two-furlong pole; true stamina and fitness become the deciding factors.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Evening Fades is so lightly pressed that she simply conserves energy throughout and outstays all challengers who struggle to close from awkward positions.
scenarios.body: With no rival able to match her from the front and the hold-up contingent failing to thread through a congested midfield, Evening Fades simply stays on for a surprise front-running victory.

watchPoints.text: Evening Fades holds a lone lead throughout — watch whether Cieren Fallon sets a genuinely comfortable tempo or allows the race to crawl, as this will determine whether hold-up horses have any chance of closing.

Lord Mayor has been off 197 days — watch the paddock closely for signs of fitness; Andrew Balding runners often show well first time back but a flat-track 1m4f on a slow surface after six months away is a stern ask.

William Buick's booking on Amrum is notable given Ollie Sangster's yard are selective with elite jockey engagements — watch whether Amrum shows any market move, as this may signal stable confidence despite the 63-day absence.

With seven horses displaced into midfield from their natural hold-up positions, watch for significant scrimmaging and traffic issues on the final bend — horses with wide draws or jockeys who can find daylight early (Buick, McDonald, Dobbs) will be at a premium.

Tinsel and Cospicua both have course-and-distance winning form on Standard Kempton — watch for either being produced with a positive mid-race move if the pace is truly slow, as they are the best-credentialled horses for the exact conditions on offer tonight.
